title: Argentinian Judge Dismisses Fraud Probe into Milei’s Crypto Scandal, Al Jazeera Reports
body:
A federal judge in Argentina has formally closed the criminal probe into President Javier Milei and his sister, Karina Milei, that stemmed from the collapse of a cryptocurrency project the president heavily promoted on social media. Judge Marcelo Martínez ruled that while Milei’s public endorsement of the digital token raised eyebrows, the evidence did not substantiate accusations of fraud or personal enrichment, effectively clearing the president of legal liability in the matter.

The investigation began in early 2024 after the “Libertad Coin” – a token marketed as a vehicle for economic freedom and touted by Milei during his televised appearances – plummeted in value, leaving thousands of Argentine investors with substantial losses. Prosecutors alleged that the Milei siblings had used their political influence to create a speculative bubble, then withdrew funds before the crash, constituting a classic “pump‑and‑dump” scheme. The case attracted intense scrutiny because it intersected with Milei’s broader agenda of deregulation, libertarian economics, and a push to modernize Argentina’s financial system through blockchain technology.

Judge Martínez, who presided over the case, concluded that the prosecutor’s dossier lacked concrete proof that the Milei family directly profited from the token’s downfall or that they orchestrated deceptive marketing practices. “The president’s involvement was limited to public advocacy; there is no evidence of personal gain or a coordinated scheme to defraud investors,” the judge wrote in a 12‑page opinion. He noted that Milei’s statements about the cryptocurrency were consistent with his ideological stance on free‑market solutions and that no financial records linked the Milei household to the token’s wallet addresses. Consequently, the criminal complaint was dismissed, though the judge left the door open for civil actions should victims pursue restitution through the courts.

Legal experts say the ruling underscores the challenges of applying traditional fraud statutes to the nascent and often opaque world of digital assets. “Regulators are still figuring out how to trace money flows on decentralized platforms, and the burden of proof remains high,” explained María Gómez, a professor of criminal law at the University of Buenos Aires. “The decision does not exonerate Milei from political accountability; it simply reflects the difficulty of establishing criminal intent in a space where anonymity is built into the technology.”

Politically, the outcome is a boon for Milei, whose administration has been marked by confrontational rhetoric and a series of high‑profile reforms aimed at curbing inflation and attracting foreign investment. Opposition parties had seized on the crypto controversy to paint the president as reckless and self‑serving, arguing that his flamboyant endorsement of a speculative token endangered ordinary Argentines already grappling with economic hardship. With the criminal case now closed, Milei can refocus his narrative on broader economic policies, though critics warn that the episode may have lasting repercussions for public trust in his leadership.

The dismissal also raises questions about the future regulatory framework for cryptocurrencies in Argentina. The government has hinted at drafting legislation that would tighten oversight of digital asset offerings, requiring clearer disclosures and stricter anti‑money‑laundering protocols. Industry insiders argue that a balanced approach is needed to foster innovation while protecting consumers, a tightrope the Milei administration will have to walk amid mounting pressure from both domestic investors and international financial bodies.

Looking ahead, the legal closure does not guarantee the end of scrutiny. Civil lawsuits filed by affected investors are expected to proceed, and parliamentary committees may launch inquiries into the president’s use of official platforms to promote private financial products. As Argentina continues to grapple with soaring inflation and a fragile banking sector, the episode serves as a cautionary tale about the intersection of political influence and emerging financial technologies. The Milei government’s next steps on regulation and transparency will likely shape the country’s crypto landscape and its broader economic trajectory for years to come.
